claims.text: Composition tuning can modify the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic HEAs.
Adjusting the concentrations of magnetic elements is a method for tuning non-equiatomic HEAs.
Fe, Co, and Ni are examples of the magnetic elements whose concentrations may be adjusted.
The relevant non-equiatomic HEAs have a disordered FCC structure.
The proposed tuning is applicable over 250–350 K.
Changing magnetic-element concentrations modifies magnetic exchange interactions among those elements.
Modified magnetic exchange interactions change magnetic ordering.
Changes in magnetic exchange interactions and magnetic ordering alter the magnetocaloric effect.
Composition tuning will produce a 20% increase in magnetocaloric entropy change relative to the baseline.
The maximum magnetocaloric entropy change will be 2.5 J/kg·K.
Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2Cr0.2Mn0.2 is an example of the fixed-composition baseline.
The relevant concentration range for magnetic elements is 0.1–0.3 atomic fraction.
The composition–property relationship may depend on the degree of disorder and the presence of defects.
The hypothesis is falsified if no tested composition within the specified boundary increases ΔS by at least 15% relative to the baseline.

contradictions.description: The system is described as non-equiatomic, but the example baseline Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2Cr0.2Mn0.2 is equiatomic.
